newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish soldiers jailed for aiding Kurd rebels.
newsitem.headline: Turkish soldiers jailed for aiding Kurd rebels.

text.p: A Turkish court on Monday jailed two army staff sergeants for seven-and-a-half years each for giving military information and equipment to Kurdish guerrillas, Anatolian news agency said.
It said the soldiers, Mehmet Peker and Ibrahim Dag, were found guilty of aiding the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebel group. They denied the charge.

"They betrayed the army they belonged to by giving information on army operations and sending army equipment to the armed bandits trying to divide the country," the agency quoted the charge sheet as saying.
Police had said the soldiers were planning attacks on natural gas installations in Istanbul and Ankara when they were arrested in August. They were later thrown out of the army.
Turkey's large army is made up mostly of conscripts but the pair were full-time professional soldiers based at two towns in western Turkey, far from the PKK's normal area of operation.
More than 21,000 people have been killed in the conflict in southeast Turkey between security forces and the rebels, fighting for Kurdish self rule since 1984.
